understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by positioning every selectable piece onto the goal tiles marked '+' at the same time; if a level had multiple goals, all had to be occupied simultaneously for a WIN, and finishing all levels would win the whole game within the per-level step budget.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_* actions to shift the currently selected piece by one 3-pixel cell ([x,y] coordinates in steps of 3). Walls ('#') and boundaries could block or alter movement; the movement_blocked flags were only hints and not guaranteed outcomes. Some objects (blocks 'B') were pushable if adjacent in the direction of motion, moving along with the selected piece when pushed, while other obstacles would prevent movement. Levels could include multiple selectables (P for the selected one, S for others); control could be switched via CLICK on the other selectable’s exact pixel coordinates (matching positions listed in objects), and clicking elsewhere (e.g., [0,0]) would have no effect.

understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by positioning every selectable piece onto the goal tiles marked '+' at the same time; if a level had multiple goals, all had to be occupied simultaneously for a WIN, and finishing all levels would win the whole game within the per-level step budget.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_* actions to shift the currently selected piece by one 3-pixel cell ([x,y] coordinates in steps of 3). Walls ('#') and boundaries could block or alter movement; the movement_blocked flags were only hints and not guaranteed outcomes. Some objects (blocks 'B') were pushable if adjacent in the direction of motion, moving along with the selected piece when pushed, while other obstacles would prevent movement. Levels could include multiple selectables (P for the selected one, S for others); control could be switched via CLICK on the other selectable’s exact pixel coordinates (matching positions listed in objects), and clicking elsewhere (e.g., [0,0]) would have no effect.
